title: Automatic drip brewing guide
scope: A published 63 g / 1,000 g reservoir-input example for an automatic paper-filter brewer rated for that batch; separate KBGV Select and Cup-One procedures must not be transferred to unidentified machines.

recipe.name: Counter Culture automatic-brewer 63 g / 1,000 g example
equipment: Automatic paper-filter brewer whose manual permits a 1,000 g reservoir-water batch with 63 g coffee
Burr grinder or appropriately ground coffee
recipe.grind_description: Medium-coarse, slightly finer than kosher salt; a texture reference, not a universal dial setting.

expected_time_s.clock_start: Pressing the machine brew switch, if recording elapsed time
expected_time_s.clock_end: Water delivery has ended and basket drainage has finished; obey model completion instructions

recipe.completion_signal: Machine cycle completes and coffee finishes draining into the receiving vessel. Power-off timing is not assumed to equal brew completion.

steps.instruction: With the machine off, check its allowed batch, filter and receiving vessel; complete required first-use flushing and seat the correct paper.
steps.why: Batch and filter compatibility prevent misuse; preparation differs between models.
steps.completion: Clean compatible basket, paper and carafe are ready; rinse water has been discarded.

steps.instruction: Weigh 1,000 g drinking water separately and transfer it from a clean jug to the reservoir without exceeding its maximum.
steps.why: This quantity is reservoir input; it does not promise 1,000 g beverage output.
steps.completion: The measured batch is in the reservoir and within the machine's allowed capacity.

steps.instruction: Grind 63 g medium-coarse, put it in the basket paper and gently level the loose bed without pressing it down.
steps.why: An even bed helps water reach the coffee; grounds need room to swell.
steps.completion: Dose is loaded, with room for swelling and no grounds obstructing the basket rim.

steps.instruction: Seat basket, receiving vessel and required lids; select the model's batch setting if present, then press brew.
steps.why: Correct assembly keeps hot liquid contained and activates any automatic drip stop.
steps.completion: The machine delivers water and coffee drains normally without overflow.

steps.instruction: Let the machine complete its cycle and the basket finish draining; keep the receiving vessel in place until flow ends.
steps.why: Reservoir emptying and delayed power shutdown do not establish the same completion boundary on every model.
steps.completion: Water delivery has ended and no significant coffee flow remains.

steps.instruction: Serve using the vessel handle, then switch off when appropriate; do not heat an empty glass carafe.
steps.why: The beverage and vessel remain hot after the cycle.
steps.completion: Coffee is served safely; actual collected output may be recorded separately.

variants.name: KBGV Select, USA 1 L table
variants.how_it_differs: 55 g coffee / 1,000 ml reservoir water, #4 cone paper, matching glass carafe with lid, full selector (8 manufacturer cups). Approximate 240–360 seconds from starting, followed by drainage confirmation. Heat is machine-controlled.

variants.name: KBGV Select, USA small batch
variants.how_it_differs: 28 g coffee / 500 ml reservoir water, #4 cone paper, half selector (4 manufacturer cups). The USA quick guide assigns half to 4–6 cups and full to 8–10. The selector does not dispense a separately measured water quantity.

variants.name: European Select dosing alternative
variants.how_it_differs: 60 g/L by volume gives 30 g / 500 ml or 60 g / 1,000 ml. This manufacturer recommendation differs from the USA 55 g/L table; it is not an exact water-mass conversion. European KBG Select operating details must be checked against that model's manual.

variants.name: Moccamaster Cup-One marked-fill example
variants.how_it_differs: 20 g selected within the older scanned Dutch manual's 18–21 g range; use #1 paper and actual reservoir fill mark. Approximately 240 seconds; machine-reported 92–96 °C. Use its compatible mug, at least the older manual's 300 ml minimum. Older manual describes shutoff after water transfer; current USA product lists delayed power-off. End by tank-empty plus basket-drained, separately from power-off. Reservoir mass, exact fill volume and beverage yield are unspecified here.

troubleshooting.symptom: Basket overflow or unusually slow drainage
troubleshooting.check_first: Stop safely, cool, then check correct filter seating, receiving vessel placement and unobstructed basket outlet; inspect Cup-One's small hole while unplugged.
troubleshooting.adjustment: If assembly is correct, try a slightly coarser grind. Follow model descaling instructions if water delivery is slow. Recheck Select batch setting.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm recipe amounts, free drainage, cleanliness and excessive hotplate holding.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Try a slightly coarser grind in the next otherwise identical batch; serve promptly.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm measured dose, reservoir input and correct batch setting before changing the recipe.
troubleshooting.adjustment: If grind is clearly too coarse, try slightly finer. Taste again before another change.

troubleshooting.symptom: Correctly brewed coffee is stronger than desired
troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm the normal model-specific recipe was followed and drainage is healthy.
troubleshooting.adjustment: For the Moccamaster procedure, add hot water to the served cup to taste.

safety: Use each appliance's manual for minimum/maximum batch and filter compatibility; a generic recipe does not approve every machine.
Keep hands clear of steam and hot outlet arms; use receiving-vessel handles.
On Moccamaster, leave required lids, basket and receiving vessel in place during brewing.
Switch off, unplug and cool before cleaning or clearing an outlet; never immerse the appliance.
Cup-One has no drip stop: keep its mug in place until coffee finishes draining.
Do not continue heating an empty glass carafe; hand-wash Moccamaster glass carafes.
Descaling and cleaner product directions are model-specific; current USA guidance advises against vinegar.

app_audit.finding: Lines 510–545 bind both batch recipes to moccamaster_kbgv_select with #4 equipment, but the live English stage text in app/src/main/res/raw/p1_exact_guidance.json:4279–4720 has no half/full selector instruction. The 1 L batch is below the model's 1.25 L maximum.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Add live model-specific selector guidance: half for the 500 g weighed-input example and full for the 1,000 g example, with explicit mass-versus-volume distinction. Keep official USA and European volume recipes separately attributed; do not call 1 L maximum capacity.

app_audit.finding: Lines 4344 and 4371 say Reservoir at 500 g mark even though manufacturer reservoir markings represent volume and cup labels.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Apply a live correction that says the separately weighed 500 g input is added within capacity; remove the invented gram-labelled mark. Preserve historical projection evidence.

app_audit.finding: Cup-One warnings already correct unplugging/cooling and wait-for-flow safety, but stage completion still inherits Machine switches off after water transfer and After auto-off from raw guidance lines 4880 and 4921. The older manual supports immediate shutoff; the current USA product describes delayed power-off.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve existing warning fixes and change live Cup-One stage boundaries to delivery ending, then drainage ending; avoid a model-independent power-switch shutdown deadline.

app_audit.finding: Lines 377–385 define automatic_single_cup_generic with cone and #1 alternatives, but the exact auto_cupone_20_300 recipe is specifically a Cup-One procedure.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Require explicit Cup-One model identity before offering its full-mark and small-outlet instructions; otherwise use only the identified machine's supported basket, capacity and cycle.

app_audit.finding: Lines 234–251 correctly make temperature unavailable as a user recommendation, time machine-controlled and the input role reservoir water. Its 1:16 default is a starting choice distinct from the exact 60 g/1,000 g recipes.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Retain machine-control semantics; display chosen recipe quantities and ratio provenance together instead of implying one universal official ratio.

app_audit.finding: Automatic drip is not an everyday BrewMethod enum value. The recipe/profile catalog is present, and grinders.json has no automatic/Moccamaster method entry.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Treat everyday-method integration and grinder/localization coverage as separate future work; use descriptive grind rather than extrapolated dial numbers.

app_audit.finding: ReservoirToEstimatedOutput defaults internalRetentionG to0.0. Generic automatic defaults use that model; RecipeCalculator subtracts only internal retention from reservoir input. An uncalibrated configuration therefore yields an expected beverage mass equal to reservoir input, without an allowance for the selected coffee-bed/protocol losses.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Keep expected output unresolved or require a justified protocol-specific model; distinguish prediction from actual measured beverage. Preserve reservoir input as its own quantity.

uncertainties: Cup-One operating instructions specify the actual mark. The USA product's nominal 0.33 L / 10 oz label and dosing chart's 0.3 L / 10 oz label are not exact conversions; no exact fill mass or output mass is asserted.
Older Cup-One manual and newer regional product pages describe different automatic power-off timing. Drainage is the completion cue used here.

The scanned Dutch Cup-One manual was downloaded from the official manufacturer link and visually read because PDF text extraction was blank. The previously cited Belgian PDF produced text/screenshot failures.

The historical 2017 SCA requirements URL returned 404 on direct opening despite indexed text. Its timing criteria were not treated as current instructions; current SCA certification announcement was read separately.
USA and European Moccamaster dose recommendations differ. Both are starting points; the guide identifies the source instead of silently combining them.
Other automatic brewers' controls, allowed batches, filter geometry and finish time need their own manuals. Generic baseline completion time remains null.
No physical brew, exact grinder calibration, appliance measurement, localization review, app execution or release validation was performed.
do_not_claim: All automatic brewers use #4 paper or support this 1,000 g batch.
A Cup-One reservoir mark is exactly 300 g, 330 g or 10 US fluid ounces in every model.
Reservoir input equals collected beverage output, or one retention coefficient predicts every machine.
Manufacturer cup marks denote ordinary drinking mugs or exact US-volume conversions.
The user must set a manual kettle temperature, bloom or pulse schedule for an automatic brewer.
An empty reservoir or automatic power-off guarantees that basket drainage has finished.
The KBGV Select half/full selector measures or halves the reservoir water for the user.
SCA certification guarantees every bean, recipe and kitchen batch tastes correct.
Decaf requires a universal 30-second shorter machine cycle.
Catalog presence proves full everyday-method, grinder, localization or physical-brewing support.
